summary.oneLiner: Neogen delivered resilient Q4FY26 core growth (22% YoY revenue) driven by volumes, while strategically pivoting capital towards battery materials with revised capex ensuring 18-20% ROCE. The imminent commissioning of Dahej (Jun-26) and Pakhajan (H1/H2 FY27) plants marks a fundamental inflection point, transitioning the company from a specialty chemical player to a integrated battery materials manufacturer with significant revenue optionality in FY27/FY28.

The imminent commissioning of Dahej (Jun-26) and Pakhajan (H1/H2 FY27) plants marks a fundamental inflection point, transitioning the company from a specialty chemical player to a integrated battery materials manufacturer with significant revenue optionality in FY27/FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 247cr (+22% YoY); EBITDA: INR 44cr (+21% YoY), Margin: 17.8% (flat despite overheads); PAT: INR 11cr; Order Book: Qualification pipeline for 6 giga-factories, provisional approvals received; Net Debt: INR 1,295cr (up due to capex funding). One-offs: Elevated finance costs from capex deployment; temporary toll manufacturing costs; actuarial credit reduced employee costs sequentially.
guidance: Standalone Revenue FY27: INR 875-950cr (ex-battery); Battery Revenue FY27: >INR 300cr (skewed H2); Margins: Targeting 18-20% ROCE on battery projects; Order Inflow: Commercial supplies expected Jul-Aug 2026 for salts; Capex: INR 600-700cr remaining in FY27.
order book & pipeline: Transitioning from pilot/qualification to commercial; 3 US electrolyte makers completed audits; 1 domestic giga-customer qualified & buying; 1 domestic mega-customer qualified for pilot; 2 additional giga-customers testing vs China; 2 more in discussion for 2027 start.
segment / subsidiary detail: Organic Chemicals: INR 194cr (+7% YoY, ~45% Bromine, ~30% Intermediates, balance Li); Inorganic Chemicals: INR 53cr (+145% YoY, volume-driven stockpiling ahead of price hikes); Neogen Ionics: INR 13cr (Q4), INR 36cr (FY26), mostly salts.
growth verticals / optionality: FY28 battery revenue potential INR 1,200-1,400cr; FY29 total revenue potential INR 2,400-2,900cr; Capacity expansion beyond current 8kT salt/30kT electrolyte dependent on demand; Semiconductor approvals for organolithium pending.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 17.8% pressured by expansion overheads, geopolitical input costs, and Dahej transition costs; Strategic pass-through mechanisms protected core profitability; Battery projects targeted at 18-20% ROCE despite INR 250cr+ capex revision due to tech optimization.
capex / expansion: Revised Total: ~INR 1,795cr (Dahej Phase 1: INR 428cr by Feb-27; Pakhajan Phase 2: INR 1,367cr by Mar-27); FY26 Spend: INR 555cr; FY27 Remaining: INR 600-700cr; Funding: INR 161cr promoter equity, INR 203cr insurance receivable, $20mn Morita JV (H1FY27).
capital allocation: Prioritizing completion of Dahej rebuild and Pakhajan greenfield; Promoter infusion of INR 161cr via preferential allotment; Final dividend INR 1/share; No major standalone capex planned post-FY27 until stabilization.
risks & watch-items: Commissioning delays (Dahej labor shortage already caused slight slip); Lithium/Bromine price volatility (though mostly pass-through); Customer qualification timelines for giga-factories; Execution risk on INR 1,800cr+ project scale-up; Geopolitical supply chain disruptions.
management quality / tone: Confident on strategic pivot and technology differentiation (Morita partnership); Pragmatic on timeline revisions (design optimization); Transparent on cost increases but firm on ROCE targets; Optimistic on non-FEOC demand visibility.
non-obvious takeaways: Capex revision driven by 'design-led optimization' and Japanese tech integration actually aims to lower long-term opex/import dependence rather than just scope creep; Actuarial assumption change artificially boosted Q4 profits by reducing employee costs; Inventory build-up was strategic pre-stocking for Q1/Q2 FY27 due to Dahej delay, not demand slowdown.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Leading manufacturer of Bromine- and Lithium-based specialty chemicals operating since 1991 (incorporated 1989), with 258 products developed by in-house R&D, 4 manufacturing sites and 2 R&D facilities.
- Describes itself as the largest importer of Lithium Carbonate in India for the last three decades, giving it direct relationships with global lithium miners and processors — a stated entry barrier alongside its specialised business model.
- Neogen Ionics is positioned as a preferred non-FEOC partner for domestic and global cell makers: provisional approvals from 4 major international customers and completed final site audits for 3 US-based electrolyte manufacturers.
- Diversified end-markets span pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, flavours & fragrances, semiconductors/electronic chemicals, specialty polymers, vapour-absorption chillers and battery chemicals; exports were 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue across the USA, Europe, Middle East, China, Korea and Japan.
- Promoters are technocrats with over six decades of cumulative domain experience; founder Dr. Haridas Kanani built India's first indigenous-technology Bromine plant and grew Neogen 750x over 35 years.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Policy] India's PLI scheme for ACC batteries carries an INR 18,100 crore outlay for 50 GWh of capacity and mandates 60% domestic value addition within 5 years, with a further 10 GWh re-bidding tranche (INR 3,620 crore outlay) and a proposed PLI for battery components that would push cell makers to localise raw-material sourcing.
- [Regulation] To claim the US 45X tax credit, US Li-ion cell producers must meet Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) rules, forcing a shift to non-FEOC suppliers with full transition expected by 2027 — the core demand driver behind Neogen Ionics' international engagement.
- [Industry] India battery demand is projected at 33 GWh (2025), 92 GWh (2027) and 236 GWh (2032), while by 2030 non-China demand is estimated at 1,125 KT of electrolyte and 141 KT of lithium salts.
- [Corporate structure] Buli Chemicals India (Patancheru) was merged into Neogen in January 2025; Neogen Morita New Materials Limited was incorporated as a 100% subsidiary of Neogen Ionics, and a JV was executed between Neogen Ionics and Morita Investment.
- [Seasonality] The business is structurally H2-weighted: European demand scales from October-November and accelerates after January, lithium-chemical demand peaks in Q4 on HVAC capex enjoying 100% depreciation benefits, and agrochemical demand follows the H2 crop cycle — management urges only like-for-like YoY quarterly comparisons.
